question.knowledge_point: Finding Points Where a Tangent Vector is Parallel to Another Vector
question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2}-2t\,,\,{t}^{2}\,,\,8t-2{t}^{2}⟩,$ find the point at which the tangent to the curve is parallel to the vector $⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t-2{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t-2,\,2t,\,8-4t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $⟨0\,,\,1\,,\,3⟩$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that ${r}^{′}({t}_{0})=c\,⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =c\,⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩ \\ ⟨2t-2,\,2t,\,8-4t⟩ & =c\,⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩ \\ ⟨2t-2,\,2t,\,8-4t⟩ & =⟨c\,,\,2c\,,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the components gives:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2t-2=c \\ 2t=2c \\ 8-4t=0\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we obtain that $t=2.$ Substituting to the second equation, we get $c=2.$
These values also satisfy the first equation. 

Therefore, $⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel only at the point corresponding to $t=2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(2) & =⟨{2}^{2}-2(2)\,,\,{2}^{2}\,,\,8(2)-2(2)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,4,\,8⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $⟨1\,,\,2\,,\,0⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the point $(0,4,8).$
